steps.text: Gather the ingredients. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease 2 cookie sheets.
Beat sugar and butter with an electric mixer in a large bowl until smooth and fluffy. Beat first egg into butter mixture. Beat in second egg along with vanilla extract.

Combine flour, cocoa, baking soda, and salt in a separate bowl; stir into creamed mixture until just combined. Fold in peanut butter chips. Drop cookies by heaping teaspoonfuls onto the prepared cookie sheets.
Bake in the preheated oven until edges are set, 8 to 10 minutes. Cool on the baking sheets briefly before removing to a wire rack to cool completely.

raw_recipe.headline: Peanut Butter Chip Chocolate Cookies
raw_recipe.description: These peanut butter chip cookies made with a decadent chocolate cookie dough are loaded with outrageously good peanut butter flavor in every bite.

video.description: Nothing better than peanut butter and chocolate! The perfect pair, these cookies balance perfectly together. Salty peanut butter and sweet chocolate, these are a go to for any occasion.

review.reviewBody: I've been looking for a good chocolate cookie base recipe and finally found it with this! I substituted the peanut butter chips for coarsley chopped Andes Mints candies (I've been looking for an excuse to use them) and they were to die for! Followed the rest of the recipe just about exactly (other than cutting back on the sugar just slightly). I baked them for 9 minutes, then finished with my "perfect cookie trick" by removing them from the oven, then dropping the pan from about 8" in the air onto the hard countertop (Seriously! Try this!), and letting them continue-cook on the hot cookie sheet for another 2 minutes before removing them to a wire rack to cool. They were crispy on the outside, moist, chewy and decadent on the inside and all-around cookie perfection! The best part of this cookie recipe is that all of the cookies turn out exactly the same size, shape and texture. These freeze beautifully in a ziplock bag to extend the "life" of that fresh-baked cookie taste, and my whole family just loved them. Just a note: Don't ruin this great cookie by using stick margarine in place of the butter (that stick margarine stuff is so hydrogenated, it's one molecule away from a plastic! lol) - much, much better with the real thing. Can't wait to try other "chips" with this recipe in the future. Thanks for the great find!

I made it as is, plus some chopped up Reese’s cups as I didn’t have a full two cups of peanut butter chips. Delicious! I scooped it into a half sheet pan covered with foil and spread it out to bake and cut into bars, so I could have smaller portions. I got 36 gorgeous, chocolatey, peanut-buttery bars and clean up is easy.

My boys loved this cookie. Changes: used half dark brown and half granulated sugar. Also let the dough sit in the refrigerator for 2 days before baking to meld the flavors. My Reeses chips tasted gross (even to my kid) so substituted Ghirardelli Caramel Flavored (rather so-so) Baking Chips (10 oz bag) and some dark choc chips. Next time: Heath Milk Choc English Toffee Bits (8 oz bag) plus dark choc chips. Then... Bailey's Original Irish Cream semi sweet baking chips plus dark choc chips. YUM!

I made a few adjustments. For one, I chilled the dough(1 hr. minimum, but I went about 3.5) and placed them on a parchment lined pan. They had the perfect combination of crisp and chewy. Total bake time was 13 minutes and cool was 7 minutes.

These were delicious melt in your mouth chocolate and peanut butter goodness! I used margarine instead of butter and came out great! I used a 1.5 TBSP scoop for the cookies to make a total of 33 cookies. I like how they had volume to them and dont go flat. I baked mine for 9 min. Will definitely be keeping this recipe! :)

Very good cookie only made a couple of slight changes. I went half brown and half sugar( 3/4 of a cup each) brown sugar makes for a moist cookie.I also used a trick from my chocolate chip cookie recipe I put the baking soda in 2 tablespoons of hot water before I add it to the wet ingredients. it makes the cookies rise a little more. They were absolutely delicious. I ate four of them before they even cooled down lol

This is my first time baking chocolate anything cookies. This recipe was simple and delicious. The cookies turned out crispy on the outside and soft, chewy on the inside. I used 1/2 white sugar and 1/2 light brown sugar. I baked for 9 minutes and let them cool on the pan before transferring them. Everyone loved them.

Scrumdiddlyumptious & very rich! Thumbs up all around at our house. The cookie is dark black & very rich (not the dark brown of brownies). I used butterscotch chips instead of peanut butter (because that is what I had) and they are delicious! This cookie goes perfect with milk or vanilla ice cream. I could see these making an outstanding ice cream-cookie sandwich. I imagine if some wanted it to be less rich you could cut back on the cocoa. Even though these are drop cookies, I rolled them very lightly (1-2x around my palms) so they would bake evenly. Other cookies I've made w/ cocoa haven't always spread the same way as a tried & true chocolate chip cookie. They came out nice & even. The recipe made 5 dozen cookies.

Wow! One of the best cookie recipes I've ever made and also my new favorite cookie. My husband and I love the pb/chocolate combo and these really hit the spot. I used Reese's brand of pb chips (my favorite chocolate brand) and they worked out nicely. I froze half the batch (form into balls and throw in a freezer storage bag) and just added a minute or two to the bake time, no need for defrosting, and they were perfect each time.

Fabulous base recipe for chocolate cookies. I used a mix of dark and milk chocolate chips and butter brickle pieces rather than peanut butter chips. Baked for 9 minutes, dropped the cookie sheet onto the countertop (tip from brightlightz), then cooled on the sheet for 2 more minutes before removing to a rack to cool completely and WOW - super fudgy cookies! This recipe is a keeper. Can't wait to use it with other types of chips.

Made this recipe last night, everyone raved about the excellent flavor of the chocolate cookie base. It’s not too rich or bland, and the peanut butter chips partner well. Today I made the same base but this time added peppermint candy cane chips and folded in some miniature marshmallows…reminded me of hot chocolate in a cookie - just in time for the holidays!
Great chocolate cookie that you can add any add in to! Definitely slam that pan on the counter when you take them out oven!
I used 2 cups of Jiffy chocolate peanut butter instead of cocoa and chips. Tastes great but I probably should use less choc-peanut butter because the batter a little runny.
Absolutely delicious! I added 1 tablespoon of esspresso power for fun. And yes, as others say, try not to eat the whole batch!
One of my favorite cookies ever!
I added 2 Tablespoons more of butter and two handfuls of semi sweet chocolate chips to make up for the "not quite 2 cups of peanut butter chips".
Great chocolate base for chip cookies! Easy and delicious as is Subbed white chocolate chips(what I happened to have) and added 1 pack of Cafe Bustelo instant espresso to deepen the cocoa flavor
These have a brownie like consistency and wonderful flavor! My new favorite!

Added (1) banana, and instead of using Peanut Butter Chips, I used regular chocolate chips. Added just a little bit of crunchy peanut butter as well since I didn't have much left in the container. Baked for 15 minutes.
